headline: Highest risk is medium: shared-file prompt injection and data leakage are limited by no filesystem/MCP overlap, while capability conflict and cascading error remain low.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ComfyUI can ingest workflow/files and Pathway is a document-processing pipeline, but both profiles show no clipboard, MCP, stdin/stdout, or filesystem read/write bridge by default. That makes direct injection unlikely and mostly dependent on unusual manual transfer or external orchestration. Uncertainty stays low because no shared channel is documented.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies ComfyUI-generated text or workflow content into Pathway inputs, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added outside these profiles, prompt injection risk increases.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable any manual copy-paste bridge between outputs and inputs.
Add a content-sanitization step before Pathway ingests ComfyUI artifacts.
Use explicit provenance labels on transferred files.
requires-engineering: add an allowlist parser for workflow metadata.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents are local-only in the profiles: ComfyUI has vendor-only egress and Pathway has no network egress, with no filesystem read/write surfaces exposed. Without a shared workspace or outbound upload path, leakage is not a default pathway. The pair still touches image/model assets on A, so any future shared storage would raise risk.
conditions: IF a shared directory is mounted for model or document exchange, leakage risk increases.
IF either agent is wrapped by an external service that uploads artifacts, data exposure becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep sensitive assets off any shared mount.
Run both agents under separate OS users.
Verify outbound network policies remain disabled for Pathway.
Restrict ComfyUI model directories to non-sensitive content.
requires-engineering: add per-directory access controls and audit logs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: No write-capable overlap is documented: both profiles have write_filesystem false, modify_git_state false, and no OAuth scopes. With no shared mutable resource or locking surface, there is no plausible capability conflict pathway in the default configuration.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same directory or repo, conflict risk would no longer be blocked.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only to shared assets.
Avoid mounting the same writable volume into both runtimes.
Do not grant shared git or database credentials.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared mutable state is introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Pathway is a document-processing framework, but its profile does not show downstream action authority, and ComfyUI does not expose a text-to-action chain here. Since neither profile documents B treating A's output as authoritative, the cascade pathway is weak and mostly requires an external glue layer not shown in the profiles.
conditions: IF an orchestrator feeds ComfyUI outputs directly into Pathway without validation, cascading errors become plausible.
IF Pathway is configured to auto-act on extracted facts, the blast radius increases.
mitigations: Insert a human review step between agents.
Require schema validation on all transferred outputs.
Log and diff intermediate artifacts before downstream use.
Use confidence thresholds before Pathway consumes A's outputs.
requires-engineering: add verification rules for generated content.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance-sensitive data class or residency mismatch is documented in either profile. ComfyUI touches media/model assets, while Pathway lists no data classes touched and no certifications or residency constraints. With no PHI, EU PII, or retention mismatch evidence, a compliance breach pathway is not established.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is introduced into either agent, compliance analysis must be revisited.
IF a deployment policy imposes retention or residency rules not shown here, the verdict changes.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents.
Document retention and deletion policies before deployment.
Separate any compliance-sensitive workflow from these tools.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls if regulated data is later introduced.
